about: Meson option sets of the Mesa builds. Until 2026-10-21 each set was the 'Build Options:' line of its recorded build (recorded_script), with -Dbuildtype=debugoptimized. Since then every set builds at the maximum optimisation of the owner's rule of 2026-10-10: -Dbuildtype=release with -Ddebug=true (optimisation 3 and the PDB), NDEBUG in the release flavour, whole-program optimisation (-Db_lto=true -Db_lto_mode=default: /GL and /LTCG, with -Dallow-broken-lto=true, without which Mesa's meson.build refuses LTO; it also appends -lto to the Mesa version string) and /arch:AVX2 in c_args and cpp_args; the rest of each set is the recorded set, in its order. 'glslang' says whether the recorded build had glslangValidator on PATH ('required' by the configuration, 'on-path', 'not-on-path'). build-mesa.ps1 passes them verbatim and fails if the new log's line differs. docs/build.md quotes them; change both together. 'release_options' and 'lab_options' come after 'options' in the release and the lab flavour only. 'compilers' says how build-mesa.ps1 -Compiler changes a set for a compiler other than MSVC. 'ships' names, per target, the file names the release ships that target as: the build writes one copy per name next to the target and stamps each with its own version resource (BD-166, tools/build/versionstamp.py), because the resource names the file it belongs to and one Mesa vulkan_radeon.dll ships both as vulkan_radeon.dll and as amdgpu_wddm_radv.dll. A target that no release ships has no entry and is not stamped.

msvc.description: cl.exe, link.exe and lib.exe of the Visual Studio developer environment. The option sets are written for it

clang-cl.description: clang-cl.exe, lld-link.exe and llvm-lib.exe of an LLVM Windows toolchain (build-mesa.ps1 -ClangToolchain), in the same Visual Studio environment for headers, libraries and rc.exe. ThinLTO in place of /GL and /LTCG, which only link.exe reads. In place of /arch:AVX2: the x86-64-v3 level (AVX, AVX2, BMI1, BMI2, F16C, FMA, LZCNT, MOVBE), tuned for Zen 2; not -march=znver2, which adds SSE4a and other AMD-only instructions that Intel CPUs do not have. -ffp-contract=off: a multiply and an add round separately, as in the MSVC build. Without it clang fuses them into one FMA, which rounds once, and NIR constant folding can then give other values than the MSVC build. -gline-tables-only: the PDB has functions and lines but no types. With full CodeView types, LLVM 23.1.2 writes a self-referencing LF_FIELDLIST for an enum whose field list needs a continuation record (VkStructureType) when ThinLTO import puts a second copy of the enum into a module, and the PDB step of lld-link then does not end (docs/build.md)

radv.description: RADV Vulkan ICD with the WDDM2 winsys, ACO only (no LLVM)

radv-mt.description: RADV Vulkan ICD with the WDDM2 winsys, ACO only (no LLVM), static C runtime (the radv set plus -Db_vscrt=mt): the ICD runs inside every game, and a game that ships an older msvcp140.dll beside its exe hands it to every DLL that imports MSVCP140.dll by name
radv-mt.recorded_script: none yet: the radv set plus -Db_vscrt=mt, first built 2026-10-01

radv-system.description: RADV Vulkan ICD for the x64 system loader (payload/vulkan/vulkan_radeon.dll): the radv-mt options, with static C runtime and NDEBUG in both flavours. The Mesa source must carry the CRT link-selection fix and the NDEBUG build fix a7f44c96. This recipe name stays because the release scripts and build records name the x64 system slot by it (BD-178)
radv-system.recorded_script: BD-178: the radv-mt option set under the existing x64 system-slot recipe name

llvmpipe-umd.description: Desktop D3D10 UMD: Gallium d3d10umd frontend on llvmpipe/softpipe, statically linked LLVM, static CRT

zink-umd.description: Native D3D10 UMD: Gallium d3d10umd frontend on Zink over the Vulkan ICD, no LLVM

zink-gl.description: OpenGL through Zink (WGL): app-local opengl32.dll plus libgallium_wgl.dll, no LLVM

zink-gl-icd.description: System OpenGL ICD on Zink (WGL): the gallium wgl target DLL renamed amdgpu_wddm_gl.dll, which the display adapter's driver key names in OpenGLDriverName and OpenGLDriverNameWow, no LLVM. The zink-gl set plus -Db_ndebug=true (no live assert in a DLL that loads into every OpenGL application), -Db_vscrt=mt (the same reason the radv-mt set takes it: an application that ships its own msvcp140.dll hands it to every DLL that imports that name) and -Dgallium-wgl-dll-name=amdgpu_wddm_gl. buildtype is release with debug info, as in every shipped Mesa component of this project: /O2 /Gw with NDEBUG, /GL and /LTCG, /arch:AVX2 and a PDB
zink-gl-icd.recorded_script: none yet: first built 2026-10-12 for BD-076, x64 and x86 (scratch/bd076-gl/out/BUILD.md)
